problem: Pretrain robot-relevant action priors from videos without ground-truth robot action labels, then adapt them to executable robot controls.
contribution: LAPA learns discrete latent actions through future-frame reconstruction, trains a VLM to predict them and replaces the latent output head for supervised robot-action finetuning.
algorithm: An inverse encoder observes current/future frames and produces VQ-VAE/NSVQ code sequences; a cross-attention decoder reconstructs the future. Label videos with these latent actions, predict them from image/language, then finetune actual-action outputs with the vision encoder frozen.
observations: Video frame pairs for latent discovery; present image and language for the policy. Future frames belong to training supervision, not deployable current observations.
actions: Pretraining codebook tokens are not executable controls. Downstream action-labelled finetuning is necessary to establish the robot-specific head and processor contract.
embodiment_and_data: Language Table and SIMPLER simulation, three Franka real tasks, robot video mixtures and Something-SomethingV2human videos. Source real setup mentions150labelled trajectories; pretraining data/context must remain separate.
experiments: Cross-task/environment/embodiment transfer, robot-versus-human-video pretraining and latent-space analysis. Generated closed-loop images in Figure7 use the learned decoder, not physical action execution.
baselines: Scratch, UniPi, VPT, action-labelled VLA and OpenVLA. Action-labelled pretraining has different supervision; pretrained models are not compared solely by backbone architecture.

quantitative_result.value: Language Table cross-task unseen: LAPA54.8±9.1% versusVPT60.8±6.6% and action-VLA58.8±6.6%; in-domain seen LAPA62.0±8.7% versusaction-VLA77.0±3.5%. Source means±standard error; not universal superiority or physical task rates.

limitations: Weaker fine-grained grasp generation, latency and limited action-labelled finetuning; camera motion can be encoded in latent actions. Qualitative latent semantics and generated object disappearance are not verified physical effects.
code_and_license: Primary fulltext examined, executable implementation/base-model/data licenses not audited. No LAPA or generated-world execution on Explorer is claimed.
hardware_adaptation: Useful video-pretraining reference only with a real target action head and measured deployment evidence. Preserve future-frame supervision boundaries, latent-versus-motor semantics and separate generated/replayed/physical outcomes.
